Subject: Aurora BYOK - key provenance & operator handback protocol

Sofia,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call last week. As we work toward the private deployment acceptance window, Aurora needs a concise description of the proposed operator handback (key custody) protocol and a short provenance checklist for the BYOK keys we will supply. Specifically we want:

- A list of what will live in Aurora's HSM vs what Redwood will manage.
- The exact steps your operator will perform during initial key import, routine rotation, and emergency key escrow (if any).
- How operator credentials are provisioned and revoked (including timing and audit trail).
- Proof artifacts we can expect post-handoff (signed attestations, envelope metadata).

I've attached our questionnaire to this thread — we need your responses to close the security review. Can you also include a short operator checklist we can run during our acceptance test?

Target: acceptance run in the week of May 24. Let me know if that timing is realistic.

Appreciate it,

Evan

Subject: Re: Aurora BYOK - key provenance & operator handback protocol

Evan —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a concise operator handback checklist and our initial answers to the questionnaire. High level summary below; see attachments for binaries and runbook draft.

High-level separation of responsibilities
- Aurora HSM (customer-controlled, on-prem): root key material, key import, unwrapping and primary signing key storage.
- Redwood: inference runtime keystore metadata, per-deployment key identifiers (opaque), and a thin KMS-agent that never persists plaintext key material.

Operator actions (import -> acceptance -> rotation)
1) Import phase (Aurora action + operator observer): Aurora imports wrapped key blobs into HSM. Redwood operator performs remote verification steps only (attestation verification, signature checks) — no plaintext exposure.
2) Acceptance phase: run the acceptance checklist (attached). Steps include health checks, attestation verification, audit log snapshot, and a signed acceptance statement (DocuSign link provided).
3) Routine rotation: Aurora generates rotated key material, wraps via agreed KEK, imports to HSM; operator triggers a metadata flip (deployment-level pointer swap) and verifies running instances pick up new key id. Rotation is performed as an atomic pointer update; no unwrapped key crosses our control plane.
4) Emergency rekey / escrow: only initiated by Aurora. If escrow required, procedure includes 3-person approval from Aurora security, operator present to execute (operator never escrows plaintext).

Operator credentials and revocation
- Operators authenticate with client certs issued by Redwood PKI bound to short-lived operator tokens.
- Revocation: Redwood will publish CRLs and a key-revocation event to the deployment's audit stream; Aurora's local route gateway will block RPC if revocation detected.
- All operator sessions are logged and signed; logs are shipped to Aurora's SIEM endpoint concurrently.

Artifacts post-handoff
- Signed attestation: TPM quote from the operator host + HSM attestation statement.
- Audit snapshot: canonical audit log slice covering import and acceptance.
- Acceptance envelope: DocuSign-signed acceptance (we'll include this in the acceptance packet).

Timing: May 24 is feasible if we have the signed questionnaire responses and access window by May 18.

Attachments: sofia_keystore_handback_checklist.xlsx, operator_runbook_v2.docx

- Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Subject: Re: Aurora BYOK - key provenance & operator handback protocol

Evan / team — quick technical clarifications from the operator/runbook side.

A few practical notes to avoid surprise during the acceptance run:
- Network: the operator agent requires a single outbound TLS connection to our control plane for health + audit shipping; all operator actions are executed via a local RPC gateway in Aurora's VPC. If Aurora wants fully air-gapped, we will run a local control-plane appliance and ship signed artifacts via SFTP.
- Key identifiers: we will only store an HSM key identifier (format: hsm://<slot>/<key-id>) and a signed metadata blob. No key material leaves Aurora's HSM.
- Rotation window: for zero-downtime rotation we recommend a staggered rollout across instances (10-20% per minute) with automatic rollback on mismatch. We'll provide a small test harness to validate rollover during acceptance.
- Attestation formats: we support standard PKCS#7 HSM attestations, TPM quotes, and a compact JSON-LD provenance record which Aurora can ingest into its compliance pipeline.

I've attached operator_runbook_v2.docx including commands, expected log lines, and the test harness script. I'll be on the acceptance call and can do a dry-run with your Cloud Ops team.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: operator_runbook_v2.docx

Evan and team —

Reviewed Sofia's checklist and Karthik's runbook. A couple of acceptance items Aurora should validate during the on-site window (short checklist for the acceptance engineer):

1) Verify the HSM signature chain and compare the provided metadata blob SHA256 with the HSM export.
2) Run the rotation dry-run using our test harness and observe application-level crypto handshake success.
3) Confirm operator cert revocation by triggering a staged revocation and retrying operator RPC — ensure control-plane rejects the request and that the SIEM receives the revocation event.
4) Confirm audit log continuity: request a signed log slice (start/end indices) and verify replay matches runtime timestamps.

If those pass, security signs off and we can complete the DocuSign acceptance. I'll be the internal approver for Redwood's side on the acceptance packet and will verify the artifacts are uploaded to the Drive link Sofia referenced.

I'll follow up with a short Confluence acceptance checklist and the DocuSign envelope tonight.

Thanks,

Monica Patel
Security Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
